docs.what_is_body: A security system inspired by Home Alone: instead of simply sounding an alarm, the app tries to deter intruders with psychological tricks — blue lights in the next room, sirens, barking dogs, or video clips of a large person in the window. The goal is for the intruder to turn back before anything happens.
docs.modes_home: Home — Default. No monitoring, no deterrence. Lights are controlled normally.
docs.modes_away: Away — Full monitoring. Kevin simulation (lights on/off) starts automatically to make it look like someone is home. Motion in a zone triggers deterrence in the reaction zone.
docs.modes_perimeter: Perimeter — You are asleep. Only sensors you have selected as perimeter (typically exterior doors, windows and outdoor areas) can trigger the alarm. Indoor motion is ignored so you can go to the bathroom without setting off the siren. Select sensors under “Zone overview”.
docs.perimeter_sensors_body: Under each zone in the Zone overview, the app lists all door/window and motion sensors in that zone. The first checkbox (without an icon) marks the sensor as active in Perimeter — typically exterior doors, windows and outdoor areas. When Perimeter is active, all other sensors are ignored. If no sensors are selected globally, all are used as before (backward compatible).
docs.entry_delay_body1: For door/window sensors you can check ⏱ to give that sensor an entry delay. When such a door is opened (in Away or Perimeter mode), a countdown of entry_delay seconds (default 60) starts before the alarm triggers — giving an authorised user entering with a code lock or smart lock time to disarm the system without setting off the siren. Recommended for the front and back door with a code lock. If the delay was started by an entry door in Away mode, hallway motion and interior doors opened on the way in do not cut the countdown short.
docs.entry_delay_body2: Tip: combine with a flow that automatically disarms the system when your smart lock reports an authorised unlock (WHEN “smart lock was unlocked with code X” → THEN “set McCallister Guard to Home”). That way the system can switch to Home mode before the door opens, and no alarm is triggered at all. The entry delay is a fallback if the flow fails or the lock does not report correctly. The flow action “Cancel running entry delay” (cancel_entry_delay) stops a running countdown without changing mode — useful in Perimeter mode, where set_mode = Home from a flow is ignored.
docs.deterrence_matrix_body1: When motion is detected in a zone, the app looks up the reaction zone in the zone matrix. E.g.: intruder detected in Hallway → blue lights + sound in Living room. The intruder thinks someone is in the living room. If the intruder moves toward the reaction zone, it is darkened immediately and a new reaction zone is activated.
docs.deterrence_matrix_body2: Configure the reaction zone and sound/video per zone under “Zone overview”.
docs.kevin_body: In Away mode, zones marked as Kevin zones are automatically activated with natural light patterns from sunset − offset until bedtime. The lights switch on/off at random intervals between random_min and random_max minutes.
docs.arming_check_body: When you arm Away, the app reports every open door/window contact sensor (event log, notification and the open_sensors_at_arming trigger). Uncheck ✔︎ on a contact sensor in the Zone overview to leave it out — e.g. interior doors that are often left open. New sensors are checked by default.
docs.escalation_body: If deterrence does not make the intruder leave, the escalation timer (escalation_minutes) runs out and the system enters ALARM mode: speakers are set to full volume and all lights (devices of class light — never plugs or appliances) strobe. The alarm_escalated trigger fires so your flows can start sirens or notify others. When the alarm ends, lights and speakers are restored to the state they had before. The alarm runs until you press Stop alarm or disarm.
docs.reliability_body: Settings are validated when saved: out-of-range values are clamped and invalid values ignored. If the app restarts during an alert it returns to the armed mode it came from instead of getting stuck. Sensors paired after the app has started are monitored automatically. A manually entered camera snapshot URL is fetched without sending any Homey credentials. The event log keeps the last 14 days, at most 1000 entries.
docs.stop_alarm_body: The “Stop alarm” button cancels ongoing escalation, sirens and deterrence, and returns to the previous armed mode (Away or Perimeter). Use it for a false alarm when you still want the system to remain armed.
docs.smart_lock_body: Use the set_mode flow card with the value Home in a flow triggered by a smart lock unlock to disarm the alarm automatically. Two important rules apply:
docs.smart_lock_rule1: Perimeter remains active — if the system is in Perimeter mode and a flow sends set_mode = Home, the command is ignored. Someone coming home late does not automatically disarm night mode. Use the “Stop alarm” button or change mode manually.
docs.smart_lock_rule2: Alarm → Home — if the system is in full Alarm and a flow sends set_mode = Home, the alarm is stopped and the system is fully disarmed (including the alarm_stopped trigger).
docs.activation_body: The alarm is only activated manually via the Dashboard buttons, or via the set_mode flow card. The system never starts automatically in armed mode after installation or a restart.
docs.flow_cards_trigger_tokens: alarm_triggered (tokens: zone, sensor, sensor_type, mode, timestamp, snapshot), alarm_escalated (tokens: zone, sensor, timestamp), alarm_stopped (tokens: zone, sensor, reason), alarm_perimeter_triggered (tokens: zone, sensor, sensor_type, mode, timestamp, snapshot), alarm_perimeter_stopped (tokens: zone, sensor, reason), alarm_disarmed (tokens: source, name, previous_mode), mode_changed (tokens: mode_new, mode_previous), open_sensors_at_arming (tokens: count, names, mode), snapshot_taken, kevin_zone_on, kevin_zone_off (tokens: zone, light_names), health_check_failed (token: offline_count)
docs.flow_cards_tip: Tip: Use mode_changed to build automations around mode changes (e.g. send a push notification when someone sets Away, turn on outdoor lights for Perimeter, or log mode history to a Google Sheet). The timestamp token on alarm_triggered gives a precise ISO time that can be included in SMS and push notifications.
docs.title_deterrence_per_zone: Deterrence per zone — how it works
docs.deterrence_per_zone_intro: When deterrence starts in a zone:
docs.deterrence_step1: The app blinks lights in the reaction zone with a slow ON/OFF cycle (default 15 sec each way). This requires the zone to have at least one device with device.class === 'light'.
docs.deterrence_step2: The event is logged to the Event Log and Homey Timeline.
docs.deterrence_per_zone_footer: 💡 in the zone header shows that Kevin mode is active for the zone (Away mode light simulation). Zones without lights don't get the Kevin mode option.
docs.media_body: These files are bundled with the app and can be used directly as a URL in Homey flows (e.g. Sonos “Play URL”, Chromecast, VLC). Copy the URL and paste it into the desired flow card.
